rulings.challenge_claim: The middle step of the row's own onset-escalation argument is byte-false: Moab is not named in the verse where the row says the second person turns onto Moab by name.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the source bytes. The consonantal skeleton of MT 48:27 carries no Moab token at all; the one nation named there is Israel, standing as the object of the derision rather than as the addressee -- הָיָ֤ה לְךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.48.27, byte tier). Inside the span the Moab token stands only at the two flanking verses (sweep: 2 of the span's 3 verses): the third-person object of the drunkenness imperative, מוֹאָב֙ (oshb:Jer.48.26, byte tier), and the vocative יֹשְׁבֵ֖י מוֹאָ֑ב (oshb:Jer.48.28, byte tier). The second-person forms at the middle verse are pronominal and suffixal only -- לְךָ֙ and דְבָרֶ֥יךָ (oshb:Jer.48.27, byte tier). The rationale's sentence therefore fails on the words 'by name', and the three-rung escalation it builds (unnamed third party, then Moab named in the second person, then explicit vocative) collapses to two rungs, taking with it the stated warrant for holding these three verses as one taunt. Everything else on the row re-verifies: all four of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses; the variant note at MT 48:27 is real (1 note, single-witness) and correctly disclosed written-against-read, and the row neither counts nor slices across it; the paseq at that same verse is real (1 seg, single-witness) and correctly disclosed count-only with no intra-verse position asserted; no parashah mark falls anywhere inside the span, so no mark disclosure is owed and the absence is not treated as counterevidence.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the clause 'a rhetorical question turns the second person onto Moab by name' with a formulation the bytes support -- second-person address without the nation named, the nation named at that verse being Israel as the object of the derision -- and re-state the escalation as two rungs (third-person object at Jer.48.26, explicit vocative at Jer.48.28). Dependent field: device_notes' sentence on where second-person address to Moab begins must be re-read against the corrected rungs, since it currently leans on the deleted middle rung. Test the cure must pass: a token-bound sweep of the Moab token across Jer.48.26-Jer.48.28 must return the two flanking verses only, and no sentence in any field may attribute the name to the middle verse. Span, unit_type and confidence are untouched; this is a prose-and-warrant repair, not a boundary change.

rulings.challenge_claim: Item one: the quoted WEB wording at three internal attribution points renders the source's curly quotation marks as straight ASCII quotes, and at Jer.48.38 additionally appends a curly closing mark the source does not carry. Item two: the rejected alternative denies any byte-attested new addressee inside the eleven-verse span while the row's own rationale identifies one, and the bytes side with the rationale.
rulings.grounds: The two items are DISTINCT defects, not one. Item two stands exactly as put and is upheld unchanged: the held-together warrant asserts that none of the internal split candidates reopens the lament frame with a fresh divine-speech formula, a woe, or a new addressee of its own, and it names the direct address to the vine of Sibmah as one of those very candidates; the bytes at that site carry exactly a new addressee -- אֶבְכֶּה לָּךְ֙ הַגֶּ֣פֶן שִׂבְמָ֔ה נְטִֽישֹׁתַ֨יִךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.48.32, byte tier), a second-person feminine singular pronoun, a vocative, and a second-person feminine singular suffix, with two further such suffixes closing the verse -- while the verse before it is first-person singular speech about Moab in the third person. The rationale concedes the direct address in so many words, so the two fields cannot both stand. Item one needs correction on two points. First, the substitution class is real and byte-confirmed, but it stands at FOUR quoted spans in this field, not three: the source's curly marks are rendered as straight ASCII twice inside the quotation of web:Jer.48.30, twice inside web:Jer.48.35, once inside web:Jer.48.38 and once inside this field's forward-looking quotation of web:Jer.48.40 -- six substituted marks over four spans. Second, the curly pair enclosing each quoted span is NOT an extra mark: it is the mandated wrapper for WEB text carrying an inline web: ref in the same field, and it is applied uniformly across every one of this field's eleven quoted spans, so singling out the trailing mark at Jer.48.38 as an anomaly misreads the convention; the only defect is the internal downgrade. Independently re-derived and confirmed: the closure formula stands at exactly three verses inside the span (MT 48:30, 48:35, 48:38), the row engages all three and correctly holds the verse-final one as corroboration because no fresh tier-1 onset follows it; the single parashah mark in the span is the SAMEKH closing MT 48:39; and there are no variant notes and no paseq segs anywhere in MT 48:29-48:39, none claimed. All thirteen of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: restore the source's own curly quotation marks inside the quoted runs of web:Jer.48.30 (two marks), web:Jer.48.35 (two), web:Jer.48.38 (one) and web:Jer.48.40 (one), leaving the enclosing wrapper pair as it stands. strongest_rejected_alternative: drop the new-addressee disjunct, or replace it with an argued statement of why a vocative to a vine is not an addressee change of the class that cuts -- the bare denial cannot stand beside the rationale's own concession. Test the cures must pass: (a) a CODEPOINT-EXACT comparison of each quoted run against the staged WEB text of its cited verse, character for character -- note that the standing verbatim-quote check passes this field clean today, because its verbatim arm normalises punctuation before comparing and its straight-delimiter arm skips spans shorter than three words, so 'the quote check is green' is NOT an adequate test for this class; (b) the repaired rejected_alternative must survive a byte read of oshb:Jer.48.32 that names the second-person feminine singular forms. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: Item one: two of the span's WEB quotations render the source's curly quotation marks as straight ASCII quotes. Item two: the novelty leg of the onset warrant is an undigited exclusivity claim the bytes contradict -- the eagle figure is neither unused nor unlike anything before it, and this unit's own second verse recurs at byte tier later in the same nations block; a second undigited exclusivity sits in the closing parenthesis about the interjection.
rulings.grounds: Distinct defects, both upheld; only the smallest leg of item two needs a correction, stated below. Item one verifies exactly: the source carries a curly opening mark immediately after the introductory clause of web:Jer.48.40 and a curly closing mark immediately before the closing attribution of web:Jer.48.43, and this field substitutes a straight ASCII mark at both -- two spans, one mark each, and the digit two is right for this row. Item two, novelty leg: the eagle noun stands at four verses book-wide by consonantal sweep (4:13, 48:40, 49:16, 49:22 -- sweep: 4 verses), so an earlier eagle figure precedes this onset; the narrower kaf-prefixed comparative shape stands at three (48:40, 49:16, 49:22 -- sweep: 3 verses), of which this onset is the first. Neither the rationale's 'unlike anything before it' nor the rejected alternative's 'unused eagle figure' names its object or carries a digit, which the exclusivity discipline requires and which no tier label may dampen. Item two, recurrence leg, independently re-derived at token level: MT 48:41 tokens 4-6, וְֽ֠הָיָה לֵ֞ב גִּבּוֹרֵ֤י (oshb:Jer.48.41, byte tier), are token-for-token identical, accents included, to MT 49:22 tokens 8-10, and MT 48:41 tokens 8-12, בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא כְּלֵ֖ב אִשָּׁ֥ה מְצֵרָֽה (oshb:Jer.48.41, byte tier), to MT 49:22 tokens 12-16 -- eight of the nine words of that stretch, broken only by the nation name (Moab against Edom), and MT 49:22 additionally opens on the same eagle-and-outspread-wings image under a different verb pattern. That is an undisclosed byte-tier recurrence inside the same nations collection bearing directly on how distinctive this onset is, and it is exactly the recurrence class that must be tier-labelled at write time. CORRECTION to the third and smallest leg: the closing parenthesis about the interjection is ambiguous rather than flatly false. Read as a claim that this interjection is not used elsewhere in the book it is false -- the interjection at MT 48:46, אוֹי (oshb:Jer.48.46, byte tier), stands at eight verses token-bound (4:13, 4:31, 6:4, 10:19, 13:27, 15:10, 45:3, 48:46 -- sweep: 8 verses). Read as a claim that it is not the woe-oracle lexeme used elsewhere it is true -- that lexeme, ה֗וֹי (oshb:Jer.47.6, byte tier), stands at seven verses token-bound (sweep: 7 verses). The sound finding is that the parenthesis is an undigited, scope-ambiguous exclusivity claim, not that it is false as written. The onset itself is NOT contested and re-verifies: the verse-initial divine-speech formula at MT 48:40 is byte-true and divine-mouthed, the SAMEKH closing MT 48:39 sits at this row's front seam and is correctly typed and tier-held, the variant note and the apparatus note at MT 48:44 are both real and correctly disclosed as single-witness, no other disclosure-bearing mark falls inside the span, the self-magnification clause is a two-verse object (sweep: 2 verses) matching at skeleton tier only exactly as the row states, and all nine of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: restore the source's curly marks inside the quoted runs of web:Jer.48.40 and web:Jer.48.43; replace 'an eagle figure unlike anything before it' with a scoped, digit-bearing formulation naming the swept object (the eagle noun at four verses book-wide; the kaf-prefixed comparative shape at three, this site the first of them); and re-cut the closing parenthesis so its object is explicit -- the interjection here is the lexeme distinct from the woe-oracle lexeme, with a digit for each. strongest_rejected_alternative: delete 'unused' or replace the leg with the digit-bearing form; the leg currently carries part of the weight against the shared-divine-speaker rival. device_notes: add the undisclosed recurrence with its tier and extent -- the eight-of-nine-word overlap between oshb:Jer.48.41 and oshb:Jer.49.22 at byte tier, broken only by the nation name -- and state how the onset's distinctiveness survives it. observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of any driver re-weighting and must be re-read if the novelty leg is dropped rather than repaired. Tests the cures must pass: a codepoint-exact comparison of each quoted run against the staged WEB text of its cited verse (the standing quote check normalises punctuation and will not catch the substitution); every exclusivity word in every field carrying an adjacent digit-bearing sweep that names its object and unit; and a token-level re-collation of the two Jer.48.41 runs against oshb:Jer.49.22 reproducing the byte-tier match. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing texture note mis-locates the book's colophon outside the collection this unit declares for itself, when that colophon is the collection's own terminal verse.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on the row's own fields plus the bytes. The device note frames this unit's terminus line as a smaller-scope model of the book's closing colophon and places that colophon well beyond this collection's span; but the row's own parent_collection field declares the collection running through Jer.51.64, and the colophon stands at that very verse -- so it is the collection's last verse, not anything beyond it. The two lines are formally kin at the bytes, opening on an identical pointed pair, tipcha included: עַד הֵ֖נָּה מִשְׁפַּ֥ט מוֹאָֽב (oshb:Jer.48.47, byte tier) beside עַד הֵ֖נָּה דִּבְרֵ֥י יִרְמְיָֽהוּ (oshb:Jer.51.64, byte tier); that consonantal opening stands at exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses). Stating the containment correctly strengthens the terminus argument rather than weakening it, so this is a fix-in-place wording defect and not a boundary dispute. ADDITIONAL, same sentence: it calls the collection's span 'dated', which no header in that collection supplies -- fold that word into the same rewrite. The boundary is NOT contested and re-verifies: the interjection opening the span is byte-true and is genuinely the other lexeme from the one cited against it, and both runs reach byte tier at their cited verses; the terminus clause is byte-attested and does close the whole Moab oracle rather than only this unit; the SAMEKH at MT 48:47 is real and correctly typed, witnessed and tier-held; the layout fold at web:Jer.48.47 is real in the staged English layer (1 continuation paragraph) and correctly held as tier-4 metadata that is evidence in neither direction; neither verse carries a variant note or a paseq seg, and none is claimed.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: rewrite the closing sentence so the containment is right -- the terminus line is a sub-unit line on the model of the book's own closing colophon, which stands at the final verse of the collection this unit belongs to rather than beyond it -- and drop the word 'dated' from the description of that collection's span. Test the cure must pass: the rewritten sentence must be consistent with this row's own parent_collection value, and any verse it names must resolve inside that declared range. No boundary change, no confidence change.

rulings.challenge_claim: Five defects, one load-bearing for the rear seam: the divine-title stack does not close the span's last verse; the closure contrast drawn against the second verse is incomplete because that verse carries both formulas; the stack is mis-counted as a two-site object; the type label calls an undated header dated; and the parashah sentence calls the mark one chapter back the nearest to this span while a mark one verse past the span goes undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Three legs upheld, two corrected. UPHELD and load-bearing: the rationale ends the span on a terror pronouncement said to close on the divine-title stack. In the bytes MT 49:5 runs sixteen tokens, the stack נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֧י יְהוִ֛ה צְבָא֖וֹת (oshb:Jer.49.5, byte tier) occupies tokens 4-7, and eight tokens follow it -- מִכָּל סְבִיבָ֑יִךְ וְנִדַּחְתֶּם֙ אִ֣ישׁ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מְקַבֵּ֖ץ לַנֹּדֵֽד (oshb:Jer.49.5, byte tier) -- matching the WEB continuation of the same verse. The stack is medial in both witnesses, so no closure formula stands at the rear seam this row cuts, and under the ruled treatment of that formula as closure corroboration only, the seam loses the closure signal the sentence implies. UPHELD: the device note contrasts the perfect-verb tag closing the second verse against the participial formula said to close the last. MT 49:2 does close on the perfect-verb tag, אָמַ֥ר יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.49.2, byte tier), but the same verse also carries the participial formula mid-verse at tokens 4-5, נְאֻם יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.49.2, byte tier), so the formulas are not distributed one per verse and the contrast fails at both ends. UPHELD: the type label reads this as a dated nation-header oracle; the header verse is a lamed-prefixed nation name bound to a divine-speech formula and carries no year, reign or month token of any shape, and it is absent from the book's nineteen classified date-candidate sites (sweep: 19 classified verses; MT 49:1 not among them). CORRECTED, third leg: the digit two is defensible, the scope word is not. The participial adonai-YHWH title stack stands at four verses book-wide (2:19, 2:22, 49:5, 50:31 -- sweep: 4 verses), of which three carry the armies element (2:19, 49:5, 50:31 -- sweep: 3 verses); the row's own span contains exactly ONE. But scoped to the nations collection the row itself declares in parent_collection, the sites are exactly two -- Jer.49.5 and Jer.50.31 -- which is the count the sentence gives. So the defect is the words 'in this span' attached to a collection-scoped count, not the digit; a ruling that the digit is wrong under every object definition omits the collection scope, and a reading that treats the count as correctly scoped ignores the field's own word. CORRECTED, fifth leg: the 'nearest' sentence is defective, but not for the stated reason. Under the source convention a parashah mark keyed to a verse breaks AFTER that verse, so the SAMEKH keyed to MT 49:6 sits at the 49:6-49:7 seam and never at this row's rear seam (49:5-49:6); it could not have corroborated this cut and is disclosed at the adjoining unit in any case. No mark falls anywhere inside MT 49:1-49:5, so nothing is owed under span-relevant symmetry. What is actually wrong is the undigited superlative: the mark before the span and the mark after it are each one verse from an edge, so 'nearest' is at best a tie -- and the writer-gate exclusivity flag standing on that very word is therefore NOT a false positive. All three of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses and the header splice is correct.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace 'closing on the divine title stack' with a formulation matching the bytes -- the stack stands mid-verse at Jer.49.5 and the verse runs on past it -- and re-state what, if anything, marks the rear seam; and replace the 'nearest mark' sentence with a non-superlative statement that the SAMEKH closing Jer.48.47 sits at this span's front seam, dropping the superlative rather than defending it. device_notes: rewrite the formula contrast so it is true of both verses (Jer.49.2 carries the participial formula mid-verse as well as the perfect-verb tag at its close), and re-scope the title-stack count by naming the swept object and its range explicitly -- two sites inside the nations collection Jer.46.1-Jer.51.64, four verses book-wide, three of them with the armies element -- rather than saying 'in this span'. literature_type_guess: drop 'dated'. observed_substrate_signals is a dependent field of the closure-claim repair and must be re-read once the rear-seam wording changes. Tests the cures must pass: a token-index read of oshb:Jer.49.5 showing the stack medial with eight tokens following; a token-index read of oshb:Jer.49.2 showing both formulas; the re-scoped stack count reproducing under a sweep whose object and range are named in the same sentence; the header verse absent from the classified date-site census; and no exclusivity word left in any field without an adjacent digit-bearing sweep. Any change to the rear seam itself would be a boundary proposal requiring explicit adoption, and is not proposed here.

rulings.challenge_claim: The out-of-span verse carrying the row's entire recurrence evidence is a doubled ketiv/qere verse in which both cited tokens are read-forms standing against different written forms, and the row discloses none of it -- nor the paseq seg and setumah at that same verse.
rulings.grounds: The variant leg is upheld and is the load-bearing one; the demand for the other two layers is over-broad. MT 49:39 is one of the book's twelve doubled-note variant verses (2 notes, single-witness) and both notes ride on precisely the two tokens the recurrence claim needs: אשוב אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שבית שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.39, byte tier) sets the unpointed written forms beside the pointed read-forms. Independently re-derived at token level: the row's own pointed trio from its own verse, אָשִׁ֛יב אֶת שְׁב֥וּת (oshb:Jer.49.6, byte tier), is token-for-token identical to the read-forms at MT 49:39, but it is NOT a contiguous run there -- the second written form stands between the object marker and the noun -- so the asserted sameness is reachable only by reading past both written forms, and under the written forms the verb is a different form of the root altogether. The row states this as a plain recurrence with neither the variant disclosure nor a tier label, against the standing requirement to tier-label every recurrence claim at write time and to check the variant inventory before counting or slicing in any such verse; here the read is the whole of the evidence. CORRECTION: the paseq seg and the SAMEKH at MT 49:39 are NOT owed by this row. Span-relevant mark-disclosure symmetry runs over the row's own span, Jer.49.6-Jer.49.6, and that verse carries no variant note and no paseq seg while the SAMEKH closing it is real, correctly typed, witnessed and tier-held exactly as disclosed. Bundling the out-of-span seg layers into the same finding overstates what disclosure symmetry requires. Confirmed alongside: the one-verse boundary itself verifies -- the discourse pivot and the verb-noun pair both reach byte tier at this unit's own verse -- and the row calls the participial divine formula closing that verse the narrator's tag without ever naming the formula object, leaving the strongest closure corroboration available to a one-verse unit unnamed.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: qualify the cross-reference so it says what the bytes say -- the idiom stands at Jer.49.39 in the two read-forms of a doubled-variant verse, each against a different written form, with the tier named -- or drop the cross-reference and rest the coda on the pivot and the mark alone. Same field: name the closing formula at Jer.49.6 as the divine closure formula rather than the narrator's tag, and state that it corroborates rather than drives, per the ruled treatment. Tests the cures must pass: the variant inventory read for the cross-referenced verse must be reproduced in the sentence that cites it (2 notes, single-witness), and the recurrence sentence must carry an explicit tier; no disclosure is required for the paseq or parashah layers at that out-of-span verse. No boundary change, no confidence change.

rulings.challenge_claim: The type label calls an undated header dated, and the internal addressee note asserts direct singular address across a verse that speaks of Esau in the third person in both witnesses.
rulings.grounds: Both legs upheld, with the second widened. First: the type label reads this as a dated nation-header oracle. The header verse is a lamed-prefixed nation name bound to the armies-form divine-speech formula and a rhetorical question about Teman; it carries no year, reign or month token of any shape and is absent from the book's nineteen classified date-candidate sites (sweep: 19 classified verses; MT 49:7 not among them). Byte-false, and because the same wrong word stands on the neighbouring header row it is a factual defect inside convergent phrasing rather than the phrasing itself. Second: the device note has the addressee narrowing from the plural imperative at the span's second verse to Esau addressed in the singular across the last three. The plural-imperative half is byte-supportable. The singular-address half fails outright at the middle of those three, which is first-person divine speech about Esau in the third person throughout -- חָשַׂ֣פְתִּי אֶת עֵשָׂ֗ו גִּלֵּ֨יתִי֙ אֶת מִסְתָּרָ֔יו (oshb:Jer.49.10, byte tier), continued by third-masculine-singular suffixes to the end of the verse -- with no second person anywhere in it, and both witnesses give reference, not address. WIDENING: the label is also imprecise at the two flanking verses of its own stated range. The first of them addresses a second-person FEMININE singular, לָ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.49.9, byte tier), not the masculine the label implies; the last sets second-masculine-singular suffixes, יְתֹמֶ֖יךָ and וְאַלְמְנֹתֶ֖יךָ עָלַ֥י תִּבְטָֽחוּ (oshb:Jer.49.11, byte tier), beside a plural verb closing the verse. So a flat singular-address label does not survive its own stated range in either direction, and with no morphology layer staged a form-class claim of this reach is a byte-checkable claim held to the same discipline as a digit -- it should be held and argued from the pointed bytes, not asserted. The boundary work is otherwise byte-sound and re-verifies: header, flee-imperative and mercy clause all reach byte tier at their cited verses; the front-seam SAMEKH closing MT 49:6 and the closing SAMEKH at MT 49:11 are both real and correctly typed and located; no variant note and no paseq seg falls anywhere inside MT 49:7-49:11.
rulings.remedy: literature_type_guess: drop 'dated'. device_notes: replace the narrowing sentence with one the bytes carry -- a plural imperative with a vocative at Jer.49.8, second-person feminine singular address at Jer.49.9, third-person reference to Esau throughout Jer.49.10, and second-masculine-singular suffixes beside a plural verb at Jer.49.11 -- or reduce the claim to what is safe without a morphology layer and say so. Test the cure must pass: every form-class label in the rewritten sentence must be readable off the pointed bytes of the verse it names, and the header verse must be absent from the classified date-site census. No boundary change: the sentence is disclosed as internal texture and no further cut is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: Item one: the span's only disclosed seam driver is a bare reintroduction of the divine-speech formula by the same speaker already carrying the oracle through the preceding span, without a disclosed addressee, scene or frame-owner change to justify treating the restart as a fresh onset. Item two: the row places a paseq at a position inside the verse in the same sentence that disclaims any position knowledge, and it assigns to Bozrah a predicate the bytes give to her cities.
rulings.grounds: The items are DISTINCT -- the first is a seam-warrant sufficiency defect, the second a pair of disclosure and gloss-extent defects inside the row's prose -- and all three findings stand. Warrant: the row's observed_substrate_signals carries the speech formula alone, with no frame-owner, addressee or scene key, and the rationale discloses no such change either. The bytes agree that none is there: the same divine first person carries continuously across the seam, from the mercy clause at MT 49:11 through the verse-initial formula כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.49.12, byte tier), where second-masculine-singular address to the same target resumes inside the same verse at וְאַתָּ֣ה ה֔וּא נָקֹ֖ה תִּנָּקֶ֑ה (oshb:Jer.49.12, byte tier), into the first-person oath בִ֤י נִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי֙ (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier). The third-person cup clause is an a-fortiori comparison, not a fresh addressee. Under the ruled internal-cut class a divine-speech-formula onset licenses a row seam WITH a frame-owner change; none is disclosed or present, and the SAMEKH closing MT 49:11 -- real and correctly located as this row's front seam -- is single-witness tier-3 corroboration that cannot supply it. The two neighbouring header rows each disclose an accompanying addressee shift; this one does not. This does NOT refute the boundary: a verse-initial messenger-formula restart standing immediately behind a parashah break is a tier-1 signal and may drive a seam. What it defeats is the sufficiency of the warrant AS DISCLOSED and the confidence resting on it. Paseq: the rationale places the mark later in the verse in the same sentence that says the inventory gives no position within it. The seg layer is count-only and intra-verse position is unsourceable, so the first half of the sentence asserts what the second half says cannot be known; the object itself is real (1 seg at MT 49:12, single-witness) and only the position words go. Gloss extent: the closing sentence names Bozrah as an astonishment and a perpetual waste. The bytes predicate the fourfold list of Bozrah with a singular verb, כִּֽי לְשַׁמָּ֧ה לְחֶרְפָּ֛ה לְחֹ֥רֶב וְלִקְלָלָ֖ה תִּֽהְיֶ֣ה בָצְרָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier), and reserve the perpetual-wastes phrase for her cities in a separate clause with its own plural verb and subject, וְכָל עָרֶ֥יהָ תִהְיֶ֖ינָה לְחָרְב֥וֹת עוֹלָֽם (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier), matching “Bozrah will become an astonishment, a reproach, a waste, and a curse. All its cities will be perpetual wastes.” (web:Jer.49.13). Both witnesses agree, so the gloss overshoots its splice. Two smaller gaps confirmed for the same pass: MT 49:13 carries the participial divine formula mid-verse at tokens 3-4, נְאֻם יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier), inside the quoted oath run and never named; and observed_substrate_signals records only the speech formula though the row argues an oath formula and a divine title as well. Both of the row's Hebrew runs reach byte tier against their cited verses, and the formula at MT 49:12 is divine-mouthed with no embedded-speech ownership question at this site.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: delete the words placing the paseq later in the verse, keeping the count-only disclosure; re-cut the closing gloss so its extent matches its splice -- the fourfold predicate belongs to Bozrah, the perpetual-wastes phrase to her cities in the following clause; and name the participial divine formula standing mid-verse at Jer.49.13 rather than leaving it inside an unremarked quoted run. A consonantal sweep for that nine-token run returns exactly three verses (49:18, 49:33, 50:40 -- sweep: 3 verses), so the two cross-references the row names are the COMPLETE set and the disclosure is not selective; the row's phrase names its tier correctly and its refusal to extend the claim into a book-wide idiom sweep is the right restraint. Two secondary checks while in the bytes, both clean. The front-seam voice shift the row rests on is byte-attested rather than translation-borne: MT 49:13 carries the oath verb בִ֤י נִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי֙ (oshb:Jer.49.13, byte tier) with the deity as its subject, while MT 49:14 opens שְׁמוּעָ֤ה שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.49.14, byte tier), a first-person verb whose subject is the reporting prophet, naming the deity separately as the source -- two first-person forms differing in subject referent, not merely in English voicing.
